passage:
Subject: I'm writing this because you asked

Dear Salma,

You asked why I vanished. I read that a topper studies eighteen hours a day, wakes at 3:30 and never leaves the desk. I copied it exactly, no changes. For three days I felt like a hero. By day six I was falling asleep over the same page. On day ten I collapsed on the bed and could not get up for the whole afternoon. I read a page and remembered nothing. Then I felt like a total failure, as if I had let everyone down. But his life is not my life; he has a room of his own and no shop to help with in the evening. I want to write my own routine now. Can we talk on Sunday?

Sunaina

qa.q: At what time does the topper wake up?
What does Sunaina feel after collapsing on day ten?
qa.a: Sunaina feels like a total failure, as if everyone was let down, though the letter later shows a wish to start again.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Sunaina use to build a personal routine, and why?
qa.a: Sunaina could track how many hours can really be studied well over a week and build from that, because a routine has to fit Sunaina's own energy and evenings.

qa.q: How might Salma see this letter?
qa.a: Salma, who asked why Sunaina vanished, gets an honest answer and an invitation to talk, so Salma may feel relieved and ready to listen.

grounding: Shows copying a topper's extreme daily routine, exhaustion within days, and self-blame though the routine never suited the person's own life.

passage: Amandeep, you asked why I disappeared for two weeks in March. I'll tell you straight. I'm Sahil. I watched a video where last year's topper described his day: up at 4, eighteen hours of study, no phone, no friends. I thought, if he did it, I have to. So I copied it exactly. Day one felt heroic. By day four I was dozing at my desk at 2 pm and reading the same line five times. By day ten I couldn't get out of bed at all, and I felt like the biggest failure alive. Then my mother said something that stuck: "That boy lived next door to his coaching centre and had no job. You tutor children every evening." She was right. His routine wasn't built for my life or my energy. Now I study eight honest hours around my tutoring, and I actually remember things.

qa.q: What time did the topper wake up?
How did Sahil feel by day ten?
qa.a: Sahil was exhausted and felt like a complete failure, unable even to get out of bed.

qa.q: What else could Sahil take from toppers without copying them?
qa.a: Sahil could borrow one useful habit, like regular revision, and fit it into a routine that suits Sahil's energy and tutoring work.

qa.q: How does Sahil's mother see the copied routine?
qa.a: Sahil's mother sees that the topper's life was very different, and gently points out it never fit Sahil's situation.

grounding: Shows a candidate copying a topper's eighteen-hour routine, burning out in ten days and feeling a failure, though the routine never matched their life or energy.

passage: I'm Abhinav, and I share a room with Jomon, so I saw it start and stop. Jomon had read an interview with the state topper, who said she studied eighteen hours a day. The next morning Jomon's alarm rang at 3:30. He printed the topper's timetable and pasted it above his bed. For about a week he looked unstoppable: books at 4, lunch at the desk, lights off at 11:30. By the eighth day he was falling asleep over his notes by mid-morning and snapping at me for making tea too loudly. On the tenth day he didn't get up at all. He lay there under the timetable and said, "I'm just not made for this." I don't know everything he was feeling. But the topper lived at home with her parents cooking for her; Jomon cooks for both of us and works weekends at a café.

qa.q: What time did Jomon's alarm ring?
How was Jomon feeling on the tenth day?
qa.a: Jomon felt defeated and hopeless, saying he was just not made for this.

qa.q: What else could Jomon try instead?
qa.a: Jomon could build a routine around his real life, cooking and weekend work included, starting with fewer hours and adding only what he can keep.

qa.q: How does Abhinav see the topper's routine compared with Jomon's life?
qa.a: Abhinav notices the topper had meals cooked at home while Jomon cooks and works weekends, so the routine never matched Jomon's life.

grounding: Illustrates a candidate copying a topper's eighteen-hour routine, burning out within ten days and feeling a failure, when the routine never fit his life.
